words.definition: your mother and father
words.example: My mum and dad are my {parents}.

words.definition: the sister of your mother or father
words.example: My mum's sister is my {aunt}.

words.definition: the brother of your mother or father
words.example: My dad's brother is my {uncle}.

words.definition: the child of your aunt or uncle
words.example: My uncle's daughter is my {cousin}.

words.definition: a boy or man who is someone's child
words.example: A prince is the {son} of a king and queen.

words.definition: a girl or woman who is someone's child
words.example: A princess is the {daughter} of a king and queen.

words.definition: a person you know and like
words.example: Tom is my best {friend}.

words.definition: a person who lives next to you
words.example: Anyone who lives next to you is your {neighbour}.

words.definition: a warm top made of wool that you pull over your head
words.example: I wear a warm {jumper} over my school shirt.

words.definition: soft clothes that you wear in bed
words.example: My {pyjamas} have a top and trousers for sleeping.

words.definition: the same clothes that all children at a school wear
words.example: Police officers and nurses wear a {uniform} at work.

words.definition: short trousers that stop above your knees
words.example: It's hot, so I'm wearing {shorts} instead of trousers.

words.definition: the season after winter, when flowers start to grow
words.example: The trees get new leaves in {spring}.

words.definition: the warmest season of the year
words.example: We have the long school holiday in {summer}.

words.definition: the season when leaves fall from the trees
words.example: The leaves turn brown and fall in {autumn}.

words.definition: the coldest season of the year
words.example: The season after autumn is {winter}.

words.definition: the part of your body between your head and your shoulders
words.example: A giraffe has a very long {neck}.

words.definition: the part of your body where your arm joins it
words.example: I carry my school bag on one {shoulder}.

words.definition: the middle part of your leg, where it bends
words.example: You bend your {knee} when you sit down.

words.definition: a pain in your head
words.example: The music was so loud that I got a {headache}.

words.definition: to push air out of your throat with a loud noise
words.example: Please cover your mouth when you {cough}.

words.definition: the part of the day from when you wake up until lunch
words.example: I have breakfast every {morning}.

words.definition: the part of the day after lunch and before evening
words.example: School finishes at three in the {afternoon}.

words.definition: the part of the day after the afternoon and before night
words.example: We have dinner at seven in the {evening}.

words.definition: the time when it is dark and people sleep
words.example: The moon and the stars shine at {night}.

words.definition: the day before today
words.example: Today is Monday, so {yesterday} was Sunday.

words.definition: the day after today
words.example: Today is Monday, so {tomorrow} is Tuesday.

words.definition: seven days
words.example: There are seven days in a {week}.

words.definition: Saturday and Sunday
words.example: We do not go to school at the {weekend}.

words.definition: sixty minutes
words.example: The lesson lasts one {hour}.

words.definition: sixty seconds
words.example: Wait a {minute}, I am nearly ready!

words.definition: the first month of the year
words.example: The new year starts in {January}.

words.definition: the second month of the year
words.example: The shortest month of the year is {February}.

words.definition: the third month of the year
words.example: The month after February is {March}.

words.definition: the fourth month of the year
words.example: The month after March is {April}.

words.definition: the fifth month of the year
words.example: The month after April is {May}.

words.definition: the sixth month of the year
words.example: The month after May is {June}.

words.definition: the seventh month of the year
words.example: The month after June is {July}.

words.definition: the eighth month of the year
words.example: The month before September is {August}.

words.definition: the ninth month of the year
words.example: The month after August is {September}.

words.definition: the tenth month of the year
words.example: The month after September is {October}.

words.definition: the eleventh month of the year
words.example: The month before December is {November}.

words.definition: the last month of the year
words.example: The year ends on the last day of {December}.

words.definition: to get something by giving money for it
words.example: I want to {buy} a new toy with my money.

words.definition: to give something to someone who pays you for it
words.example: We want to {sell} our old car for some money.

words.definition: to give money for something you get
words.example: You must {pay} for the bread before you leave.

words.definition: costing only a little money
words.example: This pen is {cheap}; it only costs ten pence.

words.definition: costing a lot of money
words.example: This bike costs a lot of money; it's very {expensive}.

words.definition: a cold box in the kitchen that keeps food fresh
words.example: Keep the milk cold in the {fridge}.

words.definition: a hot box in the kitchen where you cook food
words.example: Mum bakes bread in the {oven}.

words.definition: to make something into pieces with a knife
words.example: Can you {cut} the cake into eight pieces?

words.definition: to put different things together so they become one
words.example: First, {mix} the eggs and the milk in a bowl.

words.definition: to cook bread or cakes in an oven
words.example: Let's {bake} a cake in the oven for Mum.

words.definition: higher than most people
words.example: My dad is so {tall} that he touches the ceiling.

words.definition: nice and helpful to other people
words.example: It was {kind} of you to share your sweets.

words.definition: making people laugh
words.example: Something that makes you laugh is {funny}.

words.definition: having lived for only a short time; not old
words.example: My baby sister is only one; she is very {young}.

words.definition: quick to learn and understand things
words.example: She is very {clever} and knows all the answers.

words.definition: not afraid to do something difficult or dangerous
words.example: The {brave} girl was not afraid of the dark.

words.definition: making little or no noise
words.example: Please be {quiet} in the library.

words.definition: not wanting to work or do anything
words.example: He can do his homework, but he is too {lazy}.

words.definition: able to lift heavy things
words.example: He is {strong} enough to lift the heavy box.

words.definition: a small house made of cloth that you sleep in outside
words.example: We slept in a {tent} next to the lake.

words.definition: the place where planes take off and land
words.example: Our plane leaves the {airport} at ten.

words.definition: the place where trains stop for people to get on and off
words.example: The train is waiting at the {station}.

words.definition: time when you do not go to school or work, and often travel
words.example: We are going to Spain for our summer {holiday}.

words.definition: water that moves across the land to the sea
words.example: The {river} flows from the mountains down to the sea.

words.definition: a large area of water with land all around it
words.example: A {lake} is water with land all around it.

words.definition: a large area with lots of trees
words.example: We walked among thousands of trees in the {forest}.

words.definition: a high piece of land, smaller than a mountain
words.example: We rolled down the grassy {hill}.

words.definition: an area of land with grass, often on a farm
words.example: The cows are eating grass in the {field}.
